dedupe_keys.name: epa waste storage and staging site selection tool

description: The Waste Storage and Staging Site Selection Tool identifies and ranks candidate locations for temporarily staging and storing waste and debris after a disaster. It was developed by the US Environmental Protection Agency's emergency response research programme and is released as an ArcGIS Pro toolset, first issued in February 2021. The tool runs a site suitability analysis over a user-defined area, weighing factors such as soil type, land cover, topography, ease of transport access and proximity to surface water; users rank the criteria by importance, and the tool scores candidate areas by best fit and reports their available land area. Users can then designate sites, record their attributes and reasons, and pass them to other tools such as the EPA All Hazards Waste Logistics Tool. Coverage is the United States, for any study area with the needed geospatial layers. The code is free and dedicated to the public domain under Creative Commons Zero, with a user's guide in the repository; it needs ArcGIS Pro, which is commercial. Caveats: results depend on the quality of the input layers and weights, and final site selection still needs field checks and permits. Simulation uses: candidate staging sites and their capacity for disaster debris logistics and emergency response models. Related records: the EPA All Hazards Waste Logistics Tool (model-epa-all-hazards-waste-logistics-tool) routes waste through the chosen sites, and the EPA Disaster Debris Recovery Tool (data-epa-disaster-debris-recovery-tool) lists end facilities.
inputs: Soil, land cover, elevation and hydrography layers
